description: Pannes, fumée, urgences médicales, passagers perturbateurs, déroutements : le vocabulaire de l'imprévu.

fiches.question: Smoke, gas or vapour with a strong smell, which may be harmful.
fiches.explication: The cabin crew report fumes in the rear galley.

fiches.question: A smell like something on fire, without any visible smoke.
fiches.explication: There is a burning smell in the cockpit, no smoke.

fiches.question: Burning slowly with smoke but no flame.
fiches.explication: A seat cushion was smouldering after a phone fell into the seat.

fiches.question: Self-sustaining overheating of a lithium battery, which can lead to fire.
fiches.explication: A laptop went into thermal runaway in the overhead bin.

fiches.question: To put out a fire.
fiches.explication: The fire was extinguished by the cabin crew.

fiches.question: To get everyone out of the aircraft quickly.
fiches.explication: We will evacuate on the runway.

fiches.question: An inflatable chute used to leave the aircraft during an evacuation.
fiches.explication: One escape slide did not inflate.

fiches.question: A planned emergency landing on water.
fiches.explication: Prepare the cabin for ditching.

fiches.question: The radio call for an urgent situation that does not need immediate assistance.
fiches.explication: PAN PAN, PAN PAN, PAN PAN, we have a sick passenger on board.

fiches.question: The radio call for grave and imminent danger requiring immediate assistance.
fiches.explication: MAYDAY, MAYDAY, MAYDAY, engine fire.

fiches.question: A landing made to stop a situation from getting worse while the aircraft can still fly normally.
fiches.explication: We will make a precautionary landing at the nearest suitable airport.

fiches.question: A landing with a higher impact than normal, which may require an inspection.
fiches.explication: We reported a hard landing to maintenance.

fiches.question: The tail touching the runway during take-off or landing.
fiches.explication: We think we had a tail strike on rotation.

fiches.question: A collision between an aircraft and one or more birds.
fiches.explication: We had a bird strike on the climb out, engine parameters are normal.

fiches.question: (Of an engine failure) with parts thrown out through the engine casing.
fiches.explication: The uncontained failure damaged the wing.

fiches.question: (Of a warning) false, not caused by a real problem.
fiches.explication: We believe the cargo fire warning is spurious.

fiches.question: To look for the cause of a problem and try to solve it.
fiches.explication: We'll hold for ten minutes to troubleshoot.

fiches.question: A laser beam aimed at the aircraft from the ground.
fiches.explication: We had a laser illumination from the left, two miles from the threshold.

fiches.question: Not awake and unable to respond.
fiches.explication: A passenger is unconscious in row 23.

fiches.question: Not reacting when spoken to or touched.
fiches.explication: The passenger is breathing but unresponsive.

fiches.question: A sudden blockage of blood to the heart, often with severe chest pain.
fiches.explication: We suspect a heart attack, request paramedics on arrival.

fiches.question: A sudden loss of blood flow to the brain, causing weakness on one side or slurred speech.
fiches.explication: The doctor on board thinks it is a stroke.

fiches.question: A sudden attack of uncontrolled shaking and loss of awareness.
fiches.explication: A child is having a seizure.

fiches.question: To lose consciousness for a short time.
fiches.explication: A passenger fainted in the aisle but has recovered.

fiches.question: Having difficulty breathing.
fiches.explication: The passenger is short of breath and is on oxygen.

fiches.question: A strong reaction of the body to food, a sting or a medicine, sometimes with swelling of the throat.
fiches.explication: A passenger is having a severe allergic reaction to nuts.

fiches.question: A dangerously low level of sugar in the blood.
fiches.explication: A diabetic passenger is suffering from hypoglycaemia.

fiches.question: Losing blood.
fiches.explication: He is bleeding heavily from a cut on his head.

fiches.question: Bringing food up from the stomach through the mouth.
fiches.explication: Several passengers are vomiting.

fiches.question: An illness caused by eating contaminated food.
fiches.explication: Both pilots ate different meals to avoid food poisoning.

fiches.question: A crew member becoming unable to perform their duties.
fiches.explication: We have a pilot incapacitation and are diverting.

fiches.question: A device that gives an electric shock to restore a normal heartbeat.
fiches.explication: The crew used the defibrillator twice.

fiches.question: Trained staff who give emergency medical care, for example in an ambulance.
fiches.explication: Request paramedics to meet the aircraft.

fiches.question: The process of giving birth.
fiches.explication: A passenger has gone into labour.

fiches.question: Pressing on the chest and giving rescue breaths to keep alive someone whose heart has stopped.
fiches.explication: The cabin crew are performing CPR.

fiches.question: Feeling that everything is spinning and that you might fall.
fiches.explication: The first officer feels dizzy and is on oxygen.

fiches.question: A passenger who refuses to follow crew instructions or behaves in a threatening way.
fiches.explication: We have an unruly passenger, request police on arrival.

fiches.question: Drunk, or under the influence of drugs.
fiches.explication: The passenger appears to be intoxicated.

fiches.question: To hold or tie someone so that they cannot move freely.
fiches.explication: The crew had to restrain the passenger.

fiches.question: A physical attack on someone.
fiches.explication: A cabin crew member was assaulted.

fiches.question: Using rude and insulting language.
fiches.explication: He became abusive when he was refused more alcohol.

fiches.question: Taking control of an aircraft by force.
fiches.explication: The crew followed the hijacking procedure.

fiches.question: A warning that there may be explosives on board.
fiches.explication: The company has received a bomb threat against our flight.

fiches.question: An object that may be dangerous, such as an unattended bag.
fiches.explication: A suspicious item was found in a lavatory.

fiches.question: A person hiding on board to travel without permission.
fiches.explication: Ground staff found a stowaway in the cargo hold.

fiches.question: The police and other authorities who enforce the law.
fiches.explication: Request law enforcement to meet the aircraft at the stand.

fiches.question: To remove a passenger or cargo from the aircraft.
fiches.explication: We need to offload this passenger before departure.

fiches.question: To leave an aircraft.
fiches.explication: The passengers will disembark by the rear stairs.

fiches.question: A parking position away from the terminal.
fiches.explication: Taxi to a remote stand for a security search.

fiches.question: Expressing an intention to harm someone.
fiches.explication: The passenger is making threatening remarks.

fiches.question: To become less angry or upset.
fiches.explication: The passenger has calmed down and is back in his seat.

fiches.question: Items or substances that can endanger the aircraft, such as explosives or certain batteries.
fiches.explication: The cargo contains dangerous goods.

fiches.question: To fly to an aerodrome other than the planned destination.
fiches.explication: We are diverting to Lyon.

fiches.question: An aerodrome where an aircraft can go when it cannot land at its destination.
fiches.explication: Our alternate is Basel.

fiches.question: An approach that is abandoned, the aircraft climbing away to try again or divert.
fiches.explication: Going around, windshear.

fiches.question: A racetrack-shaped path an aircraft flies while waiting.
fiches.explication: Enter the holding pattern at ROMAX.

fiches.question: The time at which ATC expects an aircraft to leave the hold and begin its approach.
fiches.explication: Expected approach time one five past the hour.

fiches.question: A landing above the maximum landing weight.
fiches.explication: We will make an overweight landing rather than wait.

fiches.question: The fire, rescue and medical teams standing by at the airport.
fiches.explication: Request emergency services on standby for our arrival.

fiches.question: Headings given by a radar controller to guide an aircraft.
fiches.explication: Request radar vectors for the ILS.

fiches.question: The time an aircraft can stay airborne with the fuel on board.
fiches.explication: Our endurance is two hours and ten minutes.

fiches.question: The total number of people on the aircraft, crew included.
fiches.explication: We have 180 souls on board.

fiches.question: A landing the aircraft must make because it cannot continue flying.
fiches.explication: The glider made a forced landing in a field.

fiches.question: The body position passengers take to reduce injury before an impact.
fiches.explication: Brace, brace, brace.

fiches.question: To make contact with the runway when landing.
fiches.explication: We touched down long and stopped near the end.

fiches.question: To go beyond the end of the runway when landing or stopping.
fiches.explication: The aircraft overran the runway into the grass.

fiches.question: An aircraft leaving the runway surface, at the end or the side.
fiches.explication: The runway is closed after a runway excursion.

fiches.question: An aircraft, vehicle or person wrongly present on a runway.
fiches.explication: There was a runway incursion by a follow-me car.

fiches.question: What the crew plans to do next.
fiches.explication: Advise your intentions.
